agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider cancelling 2025 tax sale of West 10th Avenue properties
agenda_briefs.summary: Vancouver Council will consider cancelling the 2025 tax sale of the leasehold interest at 1208–1575 West 10th Avenue (PID 024-230-251) because no notice of the sale was given to anyone with an interest in the property, which the City calls a manifest error. The City itself was the purchaser, so no private buyer is affected. The full amount owing at the November 12, 2025 sale was $169,271.06; the heir paid $156,393.90 the next day, leaving a shortfall plus further taxes now due. The cancellation must be declared by November 12, 2026, the end of the one-year redemption period.
agenda_briefs.action_required: If you hold an interest in the leasehold at 1208–1575 West 10th Avenue, contact the City about the outstanding tax balance before the November 12, 2026 redemption period ends.

key_dates.label: Vancouver tax sale cancellation redemption period ends

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider updating Vancouver apartment regulations
agenda_briefs.summary: Vancouver Council will consider By-law 5, which amends the Zoning and Development By-law to update apartment regulations, at its October 27, 2026 meeting. Several other bylaws — CD-1 rezoning amendments for sites including 2111 Main Street, Heather Lands (South), 2110 West 5th Avenue, 2158-2170 West 1st Avenue, 1613-1625 Nanaimo Street and 2202-2212 West 10th Avenue, plus a housing agreement at 461-479 East 16th Avenue — only take effect if By-law 5 passes. If By-law 5 fails, alternative versions of the Nanaimo Street and West 10th Avenue rezonings will be considered instead.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Watch the October 27 Council vote on By-law 5, since the apartment regulation changes and several related rezoning bylaws depend on it passing.

agenda_briefs.title: Proposed: Vancouver housekeeping amendment to Area Specific Development Cost Levy By-law 9418
agenda_briefs.summary: Vancouver Council will consider a bylaw to make a housekeeping amendment to the Area Specific Development Cost Levy By-law No. 9418. Development cost levies are fees the city charges on new construction to help pay for things like roads, parks and utilities. A housekeeping amendment is a minor cleanup to the bylaw's wording or details, not a major policy change. The agenda item does not spell out exactly what would change, so builders and developers should watch for the staff report and the final wording before relying on current levy calculations.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Watch for the council decision and the amended bylaw wording — it could affect development cost levy charges on your projects.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider borrowing $175M through 4.35% debentures
agenda_briefs.summary: Vancouver Council will consider a bylaw to borrow $175 million by selling debentures — long-term bonds the city issues to raise money — at an interest rate of 4.35%. The money would go toward the projects listed in Schedule "B" of the bylaw, which is not described in the agenda item. A sinking fund is money the city sets aside over time to pay the debt back when it comes due. If approved, the city takes on this debt, which could affect future spending and property tax decisions. The bylaw has not been passed yet.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Watch for the council vote on this borrowing bylaw and any public notice of the projects it would fund.
